The Attorney General Trump Doesn't Actually Need Confirmed

Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general is dead. That's according to the senator whose vote it needs. 

"Despite comments as late as yesterday that the fund is dead, President Trump clearly intends to resurrect the payout pot for punks either by inappropriately establishing another bogus fund or pushing Congress to vote for a bill that the majority of Republicans in the Senate would be against," Sen. Thom Tillis posted Saturday. 

"It's unfortunate that Todd Blanche, who I consider qualified for the job, will not be confirmed because of this reversal."

The whiplash here is genuinely impressive. The fund is meant to compensate people Trump considers victims of political persecution. Trump said it was dead as of Thursday. 

By Saturday morning he'd revived it on Truth Social. "Todd Blanche was a voice of reason! It will immediately be back on the table, and I will get it done," he wrote. 

Tillis and Cornyn have refused to move Blanche until the fund is dead in writing. Not dead in a tweet. Now they're watching the tweet get walked back before the ink dried.

The real twist is what Trump floated earlier in the week as his backup plan. If Tillis and Cornyn won't confirm Blanche, just keep him as acting attorney general. 

Do that until both senators leave office in January. That's not a workaround for a stalled nomination. That's a workaround for the Senate itself. Run out the clock on two elected obstacles rather than negotiate with them. 

Somehow this counts as the more restrained option compared to the fund fight.

So the country may spend the next several months with an acting attorney general nobody voted to confirm. All over a slush fund that's been declared dead and resurrected twice in one week. 

Blocked by two senators who'll be gone in five months anyway. Is this a confirmation fight, or just a very expensive waiting game to see who gets tired first?

#Trump #AttorneyGeneral #Senate #Tillis #Blanche

• delayed

• incorrectly timestamped
• distorted by an outlier
• inconsistent across venues

A poor feed can turn:

a stale quote into an apparent opportunity

normal volatility into a false breakout

a temporary delay into fake arbitrage

That is why serious automation needs three separate layers:

Data quality defines what the system sees.
Decision logic determines how it interprets the market.
Risk controls limit what it is allowed to do.

Faster data is useful.

Reliable data is essential.

Because no algorithm can repair information it never received.

The model makes the decision.
The feed defines the reality it sees.

🔊 Over 3.2 million people transit through Iran borders for Arbaeen pilgrimage: Official

📌 Sanandaj, IRNA – More than 3.2 million Arbaeen pilgrims have transited through designated Iranian border crossings, as over 1.6 million have returned, the head of Iran’s Arbaeen Headquarters, Ali Akbar Pourjamshidian, says.

During a visit to the Bashmaq border crossing in Marivan on Sunday, Pourjamshidian said that no major issues disrupting the pilgrimage of Imam Hussein’s visitors have been reported so far, while urging pilgrims to distribute their travel across all Arbaeen border crossings.
​
He said the Bashmaq and Tamarchin border crossings, with their infrastructure, welfare facilities and favorable weather conditions, have sufficient capacity to accommodate and facilitate pilgrim traffic.
​
He noted that the joint services provided by Sunni and Shia mawakeb (service tents), executive agencies, governorates and municipalities at the Bashmaq crossing reflect practical Islamic unity.
​
A significant portion of pilgrim transportation on both sides of the border is being provided free of charge, he added.
​
Addressing concerns about the return journey, Pourjamshidian said efforts are underway to organize the return route, particularly inside Iraq.
​
He said authorities have designated specific locations between pillars 57 and 59, established mawakeb, installed directional signs and arranged transportation fleets to reduce difficulties for returning pilgrims.
​
Pourjamshidian said work is continuing to establish a more coordinated transportation system and designated return points to facilitate the Arbaeen pilgrimage, particularly during the return journey.
​
The Bashmaq international border crossing in Marivan has served as one of Iran’s official Arbaeen crossings for the fifth consecutive year and annually accommodates large numbers of pilgrims traveling to the holy shrines in Iraq.
